articles.title: Europe Has Already Drained 10% of Its Summer Gas Injections
articles.description: Europe has not only entered the heating season with the lowest gas levels in storage sites in decades, but it has also withdrawn in recent weeks 10% of the natural gas injected during the summer filling season, leaving supply vulnerable to potentially extreme cold winter weather. articles.title: Houthi Advance Puts Saudi Crude Exports at Risk

articles.title: China’s Coal Power Generation Slumps as Wind and Solar Surge
articles.description: China’s thermal power generation fell from a year earlier for the fourth consecutive month in October, with year-to-date thermal power output down by 0.1%, according to official data compiled by Bloomberg. In October alone, China’s fossil fuel power generation, heavily dominated by coal, plunged by 7.3% compared to the same month last year, the data from China’s National Bureau of Statistics showed on Monday. articles.title: European Gas Slumps on Milder Weather and Record U.S. LNG Flows
articles.description: European benchmark natural gas prices slumped in Amsterdam trade early on Monday as immediate supply concerns eased with forecasters expecting milder weather in the coming days and U.S. LNG flows hitting a record high this weekend. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, dipped by 3.3% as of 10:00 a.m. in Amsterdam on Monday, and traded at $96.85 (87.965 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh). articles.title: Iran Says Door to Peace Still Open after Strikes on Bahrain
articles.description: Iran targeted Bahrain for the second time in three days, the first spate of direct attacks on the Persian Gulf state in weeks, even as it reiterated that a path to ending its conflict with the U.S. remains open.

articles.title: COP31 Electrification Pledge Stalls as Developing Nations Push Back
articles.description: The COP31 climate summit may end later this week without a pledge to boost electrification as major developing countries have signaled they would not support a firm commitment, anonymous sources with knowledge of the private talks told Bloomberg on Monday. The ongoing climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, is focusing on efforts, targets, and means to raise the share of electrification to 35% of final energy consumption by 2035, the so-called '35-35 target', rather than on cutting fossil fuel production. articles.title: U.S. LNG Flows Hit Record High as Global Gas Supply Crisis Deepens
articles.description: U.S. LNG flows jumped to an all-time high this weekend as various projects ramp up production and shipments to markets in Europe and Asia that are reeling from the supply shock in the Middle East. Pipeline flows to U.S. LNG facilities surged to a record high of 21.8 billion cubic feet on Saturday, up by 12% from this time last year, data from BloombergNEF showed on Monday.
